games.title: Loop Train
games.tagline: Block-jam puzzle with a looping twist, themed around trains and their passengers.
games.coverAlt: Loop Train app icon: a yellow train running along a curved dark track against a blue sky.

screens.alt: Level 10 on a grey and green board: passenger queues on the left, a numbered tunnel and trains waiting on three tracks, with two ability slots still locked.
Level 6 on a green board: colored trains wait on three tracks at the bottom, passengers queue at stations, and two ability slots are locked until levels 15 and 20.
Level 16 on a pale blue board: a looping track with several passenger queues, a numbered tunnel and trains in red, blue and yellow.
Level 21 on a pale blue board: several passenger queues along the left and trains in many colors circling the track.
Level 26 on a snowy blue board: numbered tunnels, a frozen river crossing the map and trains in yellow, green and pink waiting at the bottom.
Level 31 on a green board: a long queue of colored passengers at the top and trains on tracks around the board, with three ability buttons at the bottom.
Level 43 on a green board: numbered tunnels on the left, trains parked on side tracks and three ability buttons at the bottom.
Level 46 on a sand-colored board: a branching track with numbered tunnels and trains in red, green and blue.
Level 50 on a sand-colored board: a larger layout with two sections, numbered tunnels, passenger queues and trains in several colors.

description: Loop Train is a mobile game that combines a looping feel with block-jam mechanics, themed around trains and their passengers.
games.role: I was the project owner and lead designer. The concept, level design, balance and monetization were mine, and I also made the graphics.

games.title: Numbala
games.tagline: Arcade math-training game for children, supporting dyscalculia therapy.
games.coverAlt: Numbala key art: the game logo above a smiling girl with purple hair in a red coat and her brown dog, with two award laurels for Indie Prize Best Game Art and Digital Dragons Editor's Choice, both 2018.

screens.alt: A small spacecraft flies through a desert-like level and fires at a target; a number strip with a highlighted 6 is at the bottom, under the caption 'Cool game that trains math'.
A spacecraft in a green forest level with the task 1 + 3 shown at the top and a number strip at the bottom, under the caption 'Add, subtract and avoid missiles'.
The spacecraft collection screen showing 'Primala' with a girl and her dog in space helmets, a star counter at 0 of 24 and the caption 'Collect new spacecraft'.
A boss encounter with a robot pirate on the right and the player's spacecraft on the left, under the caption 'Face the mean Corsair!'.

description: Numbala is an arcade game and cognitive training for children. It combines a dynamic shooter mechanic with learning math and supports dyscalculia therapy.
It was released in October 2018 on Nintendo Switch, iOS and Android and built in Unity. Today it is available only on Nintendo Switch; the iOS and Android versions have been withdrawn.
The team had 10 people: developers, artists and researchers in cognitive science and computer science.
games.role: I was the idea author and project owner. I was responsible for game design and level design, and I led the scientific research connected with the game, which resulted in a scientific publication.
